**ABOUT US:**


United Way is advancing the common good in Ventura County by providing help today in ways that strengthen tomorrow. United Way has the scope, expertise and influences to bring together human services agencies, government, businesses, private foundations and dedicated volunteers around a common vision of creating maximum impact and achieving long\-lasting results. Why United Way? We all want to have the greatest possible impact on our community and the issues that we care about. Join the movement. At United Way, you unite your hopes and strengths with others to accomplish more than any of us can alone.


**ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW:**

The mission of the United Way of Ventura County is: “To Mobilize and Inspire the Caring Power and Resources of our Community.” In keeping with this charge and in response to the shelter crisis in Ventura County, United Way of Ventura County launched a Homelessness Initiative to include a Landlord Engagement Program (LEP) to increase housing stock and utilize existing housing vouchers and housing subsidies provided by local jurisdictions and community partners in preventing and ending homelessness. Everyone needs a safe place to call home, yet that basic need is increasingly out of reach for many people in Ventura County. Limited affordable housing supply, extremely low vacancy rates, and prohibitive and rising rents, make home access for those with housing barriers exceedingly challenging. Advocating for these individuals and families includes recruiting, cultivating, retaining, and growing the number of landlords willing to help prevent and end homelessness.


**POSITION SUMMARY:**


The Housing Navigator position provides direct client support to assist individuals and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness. This role is responsible for conducting client intakes, determining program eligibility, collecting and verifying documentation, maintaining accurate case records, and connecting clients to housing and community resources. The position also assists with housing navigation activities, landlord engagement, outreach, lease\-up coordination, and ongoing housing retention efforts. Working closely with case managers, community partners, and property owners, this role helps ensure clients receive timely, coordinated, and person\-centered services while supporting the organization’s mission to promote housing stability and prevent homelessness. This is a grant\-funded position and may only be temporary employment unless other grants can continue to support the position.


**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** include, but are not limited to:


**Intake Duties:**


* Conduct initial intake interviews with clients to gather demographic, financial, and personal information.
* Explain program eligibility requirements, services, and client rights and responsibilities.
* Collect, verify, and organize required documentation (e.g., identification, income, housing, benefits).
* Complete intake forms, assessments, and enter data into case management systems (e.g., HMIS, internal databases).
* Screen program eligibility and refer clients to appropriate services or resources as needed.

**Case Management Support Duties:**


* Assist case managers with light caseload support such as scheduling appointments, follow\-up calls, and providing reminders to clients.
* Provide clients with referrals to community resources such as food banks, shelters, employment services, and healthcare providers.
* Support clients with applications for benefits or services under supervision of a case manager.
* Document client progress notes and updates in case files.
* Monitor and track client participation and program compliance.
* Assist with crisis intervention and problem\-solving when appropriate, escalating to case managers when necessary.

**Housing Navigation \& Outreach:**

* Assist with lease\-up process, as needed.
* Assist with follow\-up to property owners after housing placement and continue communication with clients to ensure housing retention. Communicate with supervisor if the client has needs that you need assistance with including mental health emergency.

* The Housing Navigator at THESSALONIKA FAMILY SERVICES will play a crucial role in assisting individuals and families in securing stable and affordable housing. This position is dedicated to providing guidance and support to clients navigating the housing market, ensuring they have access to the resources and information necessary to make informed decisions about their housing options.

* Conduct comprehensive assessments of clients' housing needs and preferences.
* Develop individualized housing plans and strategies tailored to each client's situation.

* Proven track record of working with diverse populations, including low\-income individuals and families.
* Experience in case management and developing individualized service plans.
* Familiarity with local, state, and federal housing resources and regulations.

  

Required Skills and Abilities:  

* Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport with clients and stakeholders.
* Excellent organizational and time management skills, with the ability to handle multiple cases simultaneously.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team\-oriented environment.
* Proficiency in using case management software and Microsoft Office Suite.
* Strong problem\-solving skills and the ability to navigate complex situations with empathy and professionalism.
* Knowledge of community resources and the ability to effectively connect clients to appropriate services.

jobs.description:
**About AASCSC**

Founded in 1989, the Asian American Senior Citizens Service Center (AASCSC) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the health and well\-being of culturally diverse and historically underserved communities throughout Orange County.

Enhanced Care Management (ECM) is part of **CalAIM (California Advancing and Innovating Medi\-Cal)**, California's statewide initiative to improve care coordination and health outcomes for Medi\-Cal members with complex medical, behavioral health, and social needs. Through the ECM program, AASCSC helps members navigate healthcare systems, connect with community resources, and achieve their personal health goals through person\-centered, culturally responsive care.

**Position Summary**

The ECM Bilingual Care Coordinator serves as a trusted partner for Medi\-Cal members by helping them navigate healthcare systems, community resources, and services that support their overall health and well\-being.

This position primarily serves Chinese\-speaking Medi\-Cal members while also supporting English\-speaking members as needed. We are looking for someone who not only speaks the language, but also understands the cultural values, family dynamics, and lived experiences that shape how many members access care and make healthcare decisions.

Care Coordinators meet members where they are, including in our office, members' homes, healthcare facilities, shelters, and other community settings throughout Orange County. Full\-time Care Coordinators typically manage an active caseload of approximately 25\-30 members, while part\-time Care Coordinators carry a proportional caseload based on their scheduled hours.

**Essential Responsibilities**

**Care Coordination**

· Provide Enhanced Care Management services in accordance with CalAIM, Medi\-Cal, CalOptima, and agency guidelines.

· Develop trusting, respectful relationships with members while maintaining regular contact to promote engagement and continuity of care.

· Complete Health Needs Assessments (HNAs), person\-centered Care Plans, progress notes, billing activities, and other required documentation accurately and within established timelines.

· Coordinate services with primary care providers, specialists, behavioral health providers, hospitals, health plans, community organizations, and other service partners.

· Assist members in accessing healthcare, behavioral health services, housing resources, transportation, food assistance, public benefits, and other community supports.

· Support members in identifying meaningful goals while empowering them to build the confidence, knowledge, and skills needed to manage their own health and well\-being.

**Documentation \& Quality**

· Maintain timely, accurate documentation that meets agency, CalOptima, and Medi\-Cal standards.

· Participate in ongoing training, quality improvement activities, documentation reviews, and professional development.

· Maintain confidentiality and comply with all applicable legal, ethical, and agency requirements.

**Team Collaboration**

· Participate in individual supervision, case consultations, team meetings, and required trainings.

· Collaborate with colleagues across programs and community partners to provide coordinated, person\-centered services.

· Assist with member intake, referral outreach, temporary caseload coverage, community events, and other agency activities as needed.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Required**

* Bilingual proficiency in English and Chinese (Mandarin and/or Cantonese), including verbal and written communication.
* Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional, volunteer, or lived experience.
* At least one year of experience in case management, care coordination, community health, behavioral health, social services, resource navigation, or another closely related field. Equivalent combinations of community leadership, caregiving, volunteer service, and other meaningful experiences demonstrating transferable skills will also be considered.
* Excellent organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities.
* Valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and willingness to travel throughout Orange County (mileage reimbursement provided).

**Preferred**

* Experience working with Medi\-Cal populations.
* Experience with Enhanced Care Management (ECM), CalAIM, Community Supports, managed care, or other community\-based care coordination programs.
* Experience documenting in an electronic health record or care management system.
* Knowledge of Orange County community resources.

***Summary:***



The Eligibility Specialist / Care Coordinator is responsible for ensuring clients maintain active and eligible insurance coverage throughout their course of treatment while providing administrative care coordination support. This position plays a critical role in verifying insurance eligibility, monitoring benefit status, assisting clients with eligibility renewal requirements, and coordinating with county agencies, health plans, and referral sources to prevent interruptions in services. The Eligibility Specialist / Care Coordinator works collaboratively with clinical, admissions, and billing staff to ensure compliance with SAPC, DHCS, Drug Medi\-Cal, and other payer requirements while supporting clients in maintaining access to medically necessary treatment.


***Essential Duties and Responsibilities:***



Including, but not limited to, the following described duties \- reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Other duties may be assigned.


* Verify and maintain client insurance eligibility and benefits throughout the duration of treatment.
* Monitor client eligibility status to ensure compliance with current SAPC, DHCS, Drug Medi\-Cal, and health plan requirements, including the 2027 eligibility and enrollment standards.
* Proactively identify clients whose insurance or eligibility is at risk of lapsing and initiate appropriate follow\-up.
* Assist clients with completing eligibility renewals, recertifications, and required documentation to maintain active insurance coverage.
* Coordinate with county agencies, managed care plans, Medi\-Cal offices, and other entities to resolve eligibility issues and prevent interruptions in treatment.
* Verify insurance benefits, obtain authorizations when applicable, and communicate benefit information to clinical and administrative staff.
* Monitor insurance verification reports and maintain accurate records of eligibility status and benefit information.
* Educate clients regarding insurance requirements, renewal deadlines, and documentation needed to maintain eligibility.
* Collaborate with admissions, counselors, case managers, billing staff, and leadership to ensure clients remain financially and programmatically eligible for services.
* Document all eligibility verification activities, client contacts, and insurance updates in the electronic health record (EHR) and other required tracking systems.
* Maintain accurate tracking spreadsheets, reports, and documentation related to insurance eligibility and client enrollment.
* Assist clients with referrals to community resources when additional assistance is needed to maintain healthcare coverage.
* Maintain confidentiality of all client information in accordance with HIPAA and agency policies.
* Participate in team meetings, trainings, audits, and compliance reviews.
* Perform general administrative and care coordination duties as assigned.

* High school diploma or equivalent required.
* Associate degree in Healthcare Administration, Human Services, Social Work, Behavioral Health, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.


***Certificates, Licenses, Registrations:***


* Valid California Driver's License (or ability to obtain one) and current automobile insurance.
* Background check and TB clearance as required by program standards.
* CPR/First Aid certification preferred.


***Professional Experience:***


* Minimum of one (1\) year of experience in healthcare eligibility, insurance verification, case management, care coordination, admissions, behavioral health, or a related field preferred.
* Experience verifying Medi\-Cal, Drug Medi\-Cal, commercial insurance, or managed care benefits preferred.
* Familiarity with SAPC, DHCS, Drug Medi\-Cal Organized Delivery System (DMC\-ODS), and health plan eligibility requirements preferred.
* Experience working with electronic health record (EHR) systems and insurance verification portals.
* Strong organizational, problem\-solving, and time management skills with exceptional attention to detail.

jobs.description:
myPlace Health is built around a simple but powerful belief: older adults deserve the support they need to live safely, independently, and with dignity in their own communities. As a PACE (Program of All Inclusive Care for the Elderly) organization backed by SCAN Group, myPlace Health brings together customized medical care, social activities, and daily support for participants and their families – all under one roof.


Our centers are more than healthcare facilities. They are vibrant community hubs where participants are known by name, valued, and supported as whole people. Behind that experience is a dedicated, interdisciplinary team working together to coordinate care, remove barriers, and improve quality of life for some of the most medically and socially complex populations.


For employees, myPlace Health offers the opportunity to do deeply meaningful work in a highly collaborative setting. Team members are encouraged to contribute innovative ideas, and grow alongside a mission that prioritizes compassion, respect, and impact. The result is a culture where people feel connected—to their colleagues, their participants, and the communities they serve.


At myPlace Health, work is more than a job. It’s a shared commitment to honoring what matters most.


The Regional Home Care Coordinator is responsible for coordinating home care services and related support for participants to ensure services are delivered safely, effectively, and in alignment with each individualized plan of care. As a member of the Interdisciplinary Team, this role completes home\-based assessments, supports care planning, monitors service delivery, coordinates with contracted providers and community\-based resources, and provides nursing care within the Licensed Vocational Nurse scope of practice as needed.


The role also supports participant and caregiver education, documentation, quality oversight, and day\-to\-day coordination of home care services, durable medical equipment, and related needs. This regional position requires regular travel to participant homes and work from the PACE center to support care coordination, documentation, and administrative responsibilities across assigned sites.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Coordinate home care services through contracted agencies to ensure services are delivered in accordance with each participant’s individualized plan of care, authorized service needs, and program standards.
* Participate as an active member of the Interdisciplinary Team by completing home assessments, reassessments, change\-of\-condition evaluations, care planning activities, and ongoing review of participant home care needs.
* Provide nursing care within the Licensed Vocational Nurse scope of practice, including wellness checks, medication administration, wound care, and other assigned clinical services in the home, clinic, and day center as needed.
* Monitor participant condition and home care service delivery through collaboration with home care staff and external agencies, and report changes in condition, treatment concerns, or adverse reactions to the Registered Nurse, Physician, or other appropriate team members.
* Educate participants and caregivers on in\-home care needs, safety practices, and self\-management strategies to promote participant independence, well\-being, and continuity of care.
* Respond to participant and family questions or concerns related to home care services in a timely, professional, and service\-oriented manner.
* Schedule and coordinate home care visits and support related appointment logistics, including collaboration with transportation staff to ensure timely and accurate participant service coordination.
* Oversee and monitor services provided by contracted home care agencies to support quality, consistency, and compliance with applicable regulatory and organizational requirements.
* Document all nursing care, care coordination, assessments, and service\-related activities in the electronic medical record within established timeframes to ensure accuracy, continuity, and regulatory compliance.
* Support home care operations and team effectiveness by participating in care coordination meetings, updating care plans as needed, and assisting with the training and orientation of new home care staff.

* We seek Rebels who are curious about AI and its power to transform how we operate and serve our members.
* Actively support the achievement of myPlace's Vision and Goals.
* Other duties as assigned.

**QUALIFICATIONS \& EXPERIENCE:**

* Current, active Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) license in the State of California
* CPR and First Aid certification required within 60 days of hire
* Experience providing care to frail and elderly adults
* Travel 50% of the time covering both Downtown Los Angeles \& Compton locations
* Valid California driver’s license, insurance and reliable personal transportation
* Strong verbal, written, and organizational skills
* Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment
* Proficiency in computer applications, typing, and electronic medical record systems
* Ability to maintain professionalism, exercise sound judgment, and respond effectively under pressure
* Demonstrated dependability, flexibility, and commitment to quality and ethical standards
* Compassion, patience, and respect in working with older adults and their families
* Prior experience in home care or community\-based care settings preferred

* Rapidly enrolls referrals received from offices of elected officials, community organizations, and self\-referrals, including gathering documentation needed for enrollment and creating Housing and Services Plans (HSP) in collaboration with participants.
* Conducts housing location to locate units, verify property ownership, inspects units and submits rental packets.
* Connects participants to resources that support housing stabilization and promote wellness, including medical, mental health and/or substance use services, employment, child care, etc.
* Engages households on a consistent basis to provide support related to HSP goals, and to discuss budgets and progressive financial assistance. Frequency of services will be based on the needs of the family or individual, but home visits must occur once a month at minimum.
